session: dual-camera real YOLO, two-view fusion proof, static pose

observations_same_batch.note: 3-D object: external bbox centre on the side/front, wrist on the top; external chain also has its known ~11 mm table offset

findings.coalesce_window: production 30 ms groups by receive time; asynchronous capture + 46-320 ms GPU latency never pairs the views. This run used 1000 ms. Fix: capture-time proximity or a per-camera short buffer.
findings.stale_fallback_intrinsics: cameras_fixed_target.yaml had UVC 1280x720 fx 892/cx 648; before driver CameraInfo arrived the edge back-projected 640x480 pixels with them, first external mouse observation off by (19, 99, 25) mm. Test config now uses D435i 640x480 values; config/cameras.yaml still needs the fix.
findings.gpu_reader_wedge: after several edge restarts the GPU node's external subscription stopped delivering (frames_received frozen at 47) while a fresh laptop subscriber received the topic. Restarting the GPU node fixed it.
findings.two_view_track_drift: fused target position is outside the two observations and the track drifted to (0.555, -0.056, +0.069) within 1 s for a static object. KF/table logic reacting to the inter-view offset is the next accuracy bug.

caveats: one static pose, one object, no motion
fused absolute position not yet trustworthy (track drift)
cross-view 29 mm is object-surface geometry + known external bias, not a defined-point accuracy result

run7_coalesce_experiment.latency_cost: up to ~0.6 s target-update latency; acceptable at ~1.4 fps, not for 10 Hz

open_issue: static two-view tracks drift (cup-005 ~0.5 m in 5 s); fused absolute positions not trustworthy until a per-view bias model or defined point is used
